name: Berlin
tagline: Culturally Rich EU Capital, Stability Over Arbitrage
description: Berlin is a culturally rich EU capital — more affordable than Munich, Paris, or London — with excellent healthcare, world-class transit, and a large international community. It suits FIRE retirees who prioritize European quality of life and stability over deep cost arbitrage, trading lower headline savings for security, infrastructure, and culture.

quickFacts.visa: No dedicated retirement visa; non-EU retirees use a discretionary general residence permit (§7 AufenthG) with no fixed income threshold — applicants must prove self-sufficiency and hold mandatory health insurance; path to permanent residence after ~5 years
quickFacts.safetyRating: Very safe for a capital; low violent crime, with petty theft at transit hubs
quickFacts.climate: Temperate continental — cold winters and mild summers

housing.description: Room in a WG or small studio in an outer district (Marzahn, Spandau, Lichtenberg, Neukölln fringe)

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with cheap, diverse eats out

healthcare.description: Voluntary GKV near the 2026 statutory minimum (€281). Note: a non-EU early retiree may not qualify for public GKV and should budget for private (PKV) or international cover.

entertainment.description: Museums, parks, clubs, and Berlin's free and cheap culture

1M.lifestyle: A frugal but real Berlin life — a room or small outer studio, home cooking, unlimited nationwide transit on the €63 Deutschlandticket, GKV-minimum cover, and Berlin’s famously cheap culture (free museums, parks, canal-side beers).

housing.description: 1BR in trendy Prenzlauer Berg or Kreuzberg

2M.lifestyle: A flat in a trendy central district, dining out regularly, comprehensive coverage, and easy access to museums, concerts, and Berlin's legendary nightlife. Comfortable city living in a major capital.

housing.description: 1BR in a central desirable district (Prenzlauer Berg, Friedrichshain, Kreuzberg)

healthcare.description: Income-based voluntary GKV or a solid individual PKV plan. Note: a non-EU early retiree may not qualify for public GKV and should budget for private (PKV) or international cover.

3M.lifestyle: The classic comfortable-retirement tier — a central 1BR near cafés, canals and the U-Bahn, dining out a couple of times a week, cultured leisure (Philharmonie, galleries), and a real income-based health contribution rather than the bare minimum.

housing.description: Luxury apartment in Mitte or Charlottenburg

entertainment.description: Opera, the arts, and frequent travel

luxuryExtras.description: Frequent European travel and premium experiences

5M.lifestyle: A premium central apartment, near-daily dining, top private medicine, and weekly help, with opera, the arts, and frequent travel. Upscale capital living without Munich or Paris prices.

housing.description: Luxury furnished 2–3BR in a prime address (Mitte, Charlottenburg/Ku’damm)

dining.description: The finest restaurants regularly, with occasional private-chef evenings

healthcare.description: Top-tier comprehensive private cover (PKV). Note: a non-EU early retiree may not qualify for public GKV and should budget for private (PKV) or international cover.

domesticHelp.description: Weekly housekeeping plus extra help as needed

luxuryExtras.description: Bespoke travel, art, and cultural patronage

10M.lifestyle: Uncapped luxury — a large prime-district flat, routine fine dining, top private cover, a car on top of transit, weekly help, and a generous travel-and-culture budget. Berlin is not a Zurich or Monaco price outlier, so the total lands around $11k/mo.
